open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove or refute boundary saturation for \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}\), determine any strong-duality conditions beyond the proved weak inequality, and couple the baseline-indexed occupation profiles into one predictable law-independent design and one connected honest interval.
open_obligations.obstruction: The corrected primal deliberately optimizes a different occupation profile for every baseline law. Feasibility for each baseline does not imply compatibility with a single history-dependent kernel. Moreover, monotonicity of \(w\mapsto\mathcal B_{T,\rho}(w)\) does not give right closedness or a uniform lower multiple at its generalized inverse, and the handle contains no interval endpoints or coverage calculation.
open_obligations.attempted: Replaced scalar quotas by exact occupation measures, embedded every actual adaptive design into the capacity and welfare constraints, proved the trajectory-KL identity for every local alternative through the existing Gaussian decomposition, and derived weak Lagrange duality. These steps certify necessity but do not supply the missing common-design coupling.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Evaluate \(w_{T,\rho}\) from H\"older--margin geometry, derive every local branch and flattening threshold, and construct one budget-feasible adaptive design with a connected honest interval attaining the resulting full-class width.
open_obligations.obstruction: The corrected program gives a necessary baselinewise relaxation, but its law-specific feasible profiles are not yet jointly realizable. The frozen bump lemma does not by itself evaluate the occupation program or construct the nonsmooth positive-part interval, so an explicit upper rate would still assume the central exploration-and-inference step.
open_obligations.attempted: Combined the established feasibility boundary, coverage converse, fixed-gap frontier, and bump family with the corrected occupation formulation. The new design-embedding lemma yields an implicit procedure-free lower bound, but no honest derivation converts it into a closed H\"older exponent or matching estimator.

prose_updates.tldr: An adaptive experiment that protects current participants suppresses observations from inferior treatments, while honest inference on the gain from individualized targeting needs those observations and is nonregular near treatment ties. The proved results establish class nonemptiness, the feasibility boundary, an all-procedure coverage-to-information converse, and the fixed-gap \(\rho^{-1/2}\) frontier. The corrected general construction is a baseline-indexed occupation-measure relaxation: it includes every same-context-law, off-cell-agreeing target-separating alternative, uses exact pointwise Gaussian information, and enforces stochastic context capacity and participant welfare. Every narrow honest procedure must satisfy this relaxation, and its Lagrange price program obeys weak duality. Saturation, strong duality, an explicit H\"older-local rate, and realization of the baseline-specific profiles by one law-independent adaptive design and connected interval remain open; the \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\) case remains the mandatory early kill test.

project_justification.gap: Existing regret--inference Pareto results treat point-estimation error in finite-arm, finite-feature, or finitely stratified models, while adaptive confidence-interval results generally take logging propensities as given and optimal-value inference does not price exploration by participant welfare. None combines a common observed-trajectory interval, nonregular positive-part geometry, continuous-context arrival capacity, and a hard uniform welfare budget. The remaining gap is not a missing scalar allocation formula: it is saturation and common sequential realization of baseline-indexed occupation profiles.
project_justification.niche: The targeting gain \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\) combines a regular benchmark term with a nonsmooth positive-part term. A welfare budget makes information endogenous because an arm's local information is integrated against a context-dependent occupation measure while its cost is the baseline gap. This produces a baseline-indexed sequential modulus with stochastic context-capacity constraints.
project_justification.fill: The procedure-free coverage theorem converts target separation and adaptive Gaussian information into a lower bound for every design and interval. The corrected local sets include all same-context-law alternatives agreeing off a cell whose target separation exceeds \(2w/(1-2\delta)\), without a sign-switch restriction. Arm-specific occupation measures yield the exact information integral; the global primal enforces context-arrival domination and welfare cost before taking the worst baseline. A Lagrange price program has proved weak duality, and every honest width-\(w\) procedure induces a primal-feasible profile, giving \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\). The open kernel is to evaluate and saturate this implicit width and to realize its baseline-specific profiles by one predictable design and connected honest interval.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No attaining nuisance estimator is currently part of the core. The corrected object is an occupation-measure relaxation. Any upper theorem must explicitly construct predictable regression or approximation estimates, interval endpoints, bias control, and coverage from the realized adaptive sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Perchet and Rigollet supply the cited H\"older--margin regret exponent used only for the feasibility boundary. Simchi-Levi and Wang establish a finite-arm regret--estimation frontier, and Li, Shi, and Simchi-Levi balance regret and CATE error over finitely many contexts; neither resolves continuous-context honest width under a hard welfare budget. Hu, Kallus, and Mao motivate selective local exploration, while Hadad and coauthors, Bibaut and coauthors, Waudby-Smith and coauthors, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas, and Shen and coauthors provide adaptive-score or stability tools when the logging design or regular target is supplied. Luedtke and van der Laan and Ponomarev and Semenova address nonregular optimal-welfare inference without optimizing welfare-constrained data collection. Kaufmann, Capp\'e, and Garivier support the adaptive Gaussian change-of-measure step, and Cai and Low support the coverage-to-length logic. None of these sources proves saturation, strong duality, or law-independent sequential realization for the corrected baseline-indexed occupation relaxation; those claims remain open rather than being imported from prior work.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The occupation program is a necessary baselinewise relaxation, not an estimator. Its inner optimizer may depend on the unknown baseline law, and separate feasible profiles need not be compatible with one predictable law-independent design. Monotonicity alone does not control a jump at \(w_{T,\rho}\), and weak duality alone does not yield strong duality or attainment. The bump lemma and regret packing do not by themselves evaluate the scalar targeting-gain width because target contributions can cancel and adaptive allocation can concentrate on selected contexts.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established scope consists of class nonemptiness, the cited feasibility exponent with its Gaussian transfer, the all-design coverage--information converse, the fixed-gap \(\rho^{-1/2}\) theorem, the target-separating bump construction, weak duality for the corrected occupation programs, and the necessary bounds \(\Omega_{T,\delta}\ge2w_{T,\rho}/(1-2\delta)\) and \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\). The width and modulus equal \(+\infty\) when the uniformly feasible design class is empty. The exact H\"older-local rate, saturation and boundary regularity of \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}\), strong duality or attainment, and realization by one predictable design and connected interval remain answer-open. At \(\rho\asymp T\), a completed result must recover fixed-design honest inference; on the fixed-gap subclass it must recover \(\rho^{-1/2}\); below \(T^{r_{\beta,\alpha,d}}\), the design class is empty.
